hob_001: You can recognise it as the one evergreen tree holding the fourth corner of the intersection, a seedling of its own now growing beside it. It stands outside St David's Cathedral.
hob_003: You can recognise it by its trunk forking into two co-dominant leaders under a stack of horizontal branch tiers. It stands outside Ingle Hall, Macquarie and Argyle Streets.
hob_004: You can recognise it by its dark green, cone-shaped column running straight up out of the footpath. It stands at 67 Brisbane Street.
hob_008: You can recognise it by its long, drooping needles giving it a loose, shaggy look, closer to a green waterfall than a stiff pine. It stands in the pinetum of the Botanical Gardens.
hob_009: You can recognise it as the one specific oak the city registered among several in the gardens, near the main house and glasshouse complex. It stands in the Royal Tasmanian Botanical Gardens.
hob_010: You can recognise it by its bark, shedding in irregular patches to leave a trunk mottled grey, cream, olive and pink. It stands in the Royal Tasmanian Botanical Gardens.
hob_011: You can recognise it as Australia's tallest tree, its trunk 12 metres round with a hollow burned into the base by the 2019 fires. It stands deep in the Arve Valley.
